text: Ulta Beauty, Inc. is the largest specialty beauty retailer in the United States and the premier destination for cosmetics, fragrance, skincare, haircare, and salon services. The company offers a unique assortment of over 25,000 products from more than 600 beauty brands across various categories and price points, including prestige and mass cosmetics, fragrance, haircare, skincare, bath and body products, professional hair products, and salon styling tools. Ulta operates more than 1,350 stores, primarily in high-traffic, convenient locations, with a bright and open store design that allows for flexibility in responding to consumer trends. Nearly every store provides beauty services, including a full-service hair salon and a Benefit™ Brow Bar. Additionally, the company has over 350 Ulta Beauty at Target shop-in-shops located in 1,000 square feet of dedicated space within Target locations, offering a curated, premium beauty experience. Through its website, Ulta.com, and mobile applications, Ulta delivers convenient, interactive, and personalized digital experiences, including virtual try-on and skin analysis tools using augmented reality and artificial intelligence. The company’s Ultamate Rewards loyalty program, which accounts for more than 95% of total sales, enables members to earn points on purchases at Ulta Beauty, through private label and co-branded credit cards, and at Ulta Beauty at Target, with points redeemable for discounts on products and services. With over 40.2 million active members, Ulta has deep insights into customer preferences, allowing for personalized experiences and promotions via its Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform. Ulta defines its target consumer as a beauty enthusiast—someone passionate about beauty, using it for self-expression and self-investment—who represents approximately 65% of shoppers and accounts for over 80% of U.S. beauty product and service spending. The company’s strategy centers on six key pillars: expanding the definition of All Things Beauty by growing in core categories like makeup, skincare, and fragrance, developing cross-category platforms such as Conscious Beauty, Black-owned and BIPOC-founded brands, the Wellness Shop, and SPARKED at Ulta Beauty, offering exclusive private label products, and improving profitability through inventory and promotional optimization; evolving the omnichannel experience through a connected physical and digital ecosystem, All In Your World, by expanding store footprints, enhancing digital experiences, and enabling buy anywhere, fill anywhere capabilities; deepening its presence across the beauty journey by amplifying brand purpose, building a creator and content ecosystem, innovating the loyalty program, and using member data to personalize offerings and increase engagement; and driving operational excellence through continuous improvement, Project SOAR (its new enterprise resource planning platform), and supply chain optimization. The company was founded in 1990 and initially differentiated itself by offering a broad range of beauty products and services in a single, welcoming retail environment, which has since evolved to meet changing consumer behaviors. Despite ongoing challenges such as rising labor and transportation costs, and the lingering effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, Ulta continues to see strong consumer engagement in both physical and digital channels. The aggregate market value of the company’s voting stock held by non-affiliates, based on the closing price on July 29, 2022, was approximately $16,116,323,000. As of March 20, 2023, the company had 50,195,089 shares of common stock, par value $0.01 per share, outstanding. The registrant is a well-known seasoned issuer and has filed all required reports under Section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 during the prior 12 months and for the past 90 days. Information in Part III of the Form 10-K is incorporated by reference from the registrant’s 2023 Annual Meeting of Stockholders Proxy Statement, which will be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission within 120 days of the fiscal year ended January 28, 2023.

Ulta Beauty has developed a robust consumer research capability that leverages both behavioral insights and real-time data, with over 95% of total sales coming from its 40.2 million active Ultamate Rewards loyalty program members, providing deep insights into customer preferences and behavior. Beauty enthusiasts are shown to have an emotional, personal, and deep connection with beauty, which is amplified by social media engagement, and Ulta Beauty expects this influence to grow as social platform usage increases. To enhance reach, relevancy, and guest engagement, the company plans to amplify its brand purpose, build a creator and content ecosystem to deliver compelling, relevant beauty entertainment, drive innovation in the Ultamate Rewards program, and use member data to increase personalization, drive conversion, and support its brands. The company’s vision is to expand and deepen its presence across the beauty journey to increase consumer acquisition and drive guest engagement, loyalty, and share of wallet. To address persistent cost pressures from macroeconomic trends such as rising wages, higher transportation and shipping costs, and channel and category mix shifts, Ulta Beauty has established a continuous improvement capability to identify cross-functional process optimizations, upgraded its enterprise resource planning platform to improve efficiency and support future growth, and enhanced its supply chain network to increase agility, speed, and cost-efficiency, aiming to deliver profitable growth and competitive advantage through cost optimization, agile operations, and new omnichannel capabilities. Ulta Beauty has cultivated a guest and associate-centric, values-based, high-performance culture that emphasizes collaboration, enterprise thinking, and listening to associates for continuous improvement, supported by an experienced leadership team and passionate associates committed to living its values. The company is committed to expanding its environmental and social impact by promoting inclusivity in beauty for all ages, sizes, abilities, skin tones, cultures, and genders, and by empowering guests to make informed, sustainable choices through its Conscious Beauty at Ulta Beauty® platform, which certifies brands in Clean Ingredients, Cruelty Free, Vegan, and Sustainable Packaging, with over 300 brands participating as of January 28, 2023, and more than half certified in multiple pillars. The program launched with 187 brands and includes a “Made Without List” and a Conscious Beauty Advisory Council to guide its evolution. Ulta Beauty operates in the U.S. beauty products and salon services industry, which in 2022 represented $172 billion in sales, with beauty products totaling $104 billion and salon services totaling $68 billion. Ulta Beauty holds an estimated 9% share of the beauty products market and less than 1% share of the salon services market. It competes across all major categories and price points with prestige, mass, and salon products, and offers full-service hair salons in most stores, brow bars in most, and makeup services through salons, with skin services available in approximately 150 locations. In fiscal 2022, 76% of loyalty members transacted solely in physical stores, and the company has a retail store concept that has evolved to meet guest expectations, with typical stores being approximately 10,000 square feet, including about 950 square feet dedicated to salons. Store data shows that from January 28, 2023, to January 30, 2021, the total number of stores increased from 1,308 to 1,355, with 47 stores opened, 4 closed, and 20 stores closed in 2021, and a total square footage increase from 13,291,838 to 14,200,403, with an average store size of 10,480 square feet. The company remodeled 20 stores in fiscal 2023, 9 in 2022, and relocated 12 in 2023, 7 in 2022, and 5 in 2021. Ulta Beauty aims to grow its store footprint to between 1,500 and 1,700 freestanding stores in the U.S. and uses beauty market share data and loyalty member insights to select and optimize store locations, with an average net investment of $1.7 million per new store, including capital, pre-opening expenses, and initial inventory. A new store layout, which organizes categories by prestige to mass with intuitive adjacencies and features like elevated gondolas and Beauty Bars, is being introduced to better reflect how guests shop and simplify exploration. In fiscal 2022, 17% of loyalty members shopped both in stores and through digital platforms, and the e-commerce platform supports direct sales and drives traffic to stores, the website, and apps, with omnichannel guests spending nearly three times as much as retail-only guests. Ulta Beauty is improving order fulfillment with faster delivery through distribution centers, fast fulfillment centers, select retail stores, and a new market fulfillment center starting in 2023, and offers “Buy Online, Pick-up in Store,” “Curbside Pickup,” “Store 2 Door,” and same-day delivery in select markets. The company has a long-term partnership with Target Corporation to launch Ulta Beauty at Target, a “shop-in-shop” concept with over 60 prestige brands in 1,000 square feet of space, staffed by Target team members trained by Ulta Beauty, where loyalty members earn points (but not redeem) and can only redeem points in Ulta Beauty stores, on Ulta.com, or via mobile apps. As of January 28, 2023, Ulta Beauty at Target was available in over 350 Target locations and on target.com, with a goal of being in up to 800 locations. Ulta Beauty offers over 25,000 products from more than 600 brands across all categories and price points, including its private label, the Ulta Beauty Collection, and exclusive products such as Tarte Double Duty Beauty, IT Brushes, and CHI for Ulta Beauty. The Ulta Beauty Collection and permanent exclusives represented 4% of total net sales in fiscal 2022, while both permanent and temporary exclusives represented 10% of total net sales. The company offers a balanced portfolio across six categories: cosmetics (42% in 2023, 43% in 2022, 45% in 2021), haircare products and styling tools (21%, 20%, 20%), skincare (17%, 17%, 16%), fragrance and bath (14%, 14%, 12%), services (3%, 3%, 3%), and accessories and other (3%, 3%, 4%). The merchandising team is led by a Chief Merchandising Officer who oversees category vice presidents, divisional merchandise managers, and a centralized planning and forecasting group, and uses centrally produced planograms and promotional merchandising planners to guide product placement, with regular revisions based on sales trends. The visual team collaborates with merchandising to develop strategic placements for promotional merchandise, signage, and product education. Ulta Beauty has increased its assortment of Black-owned and Black-founded brands by 34% in fiscal 2022, adding 12 such brands, as part of a commitment to dedicate 15% of its brand assortment to these brands over time.

Our merchandising team is led by a Chief Merchandising Officer who oversees Senior Vice Presidents of Cosmetics and category Vice Presidents, who in turn manage Divisional Merchandise Managers and their buyer teams. The Chief Merchandising Officer also leads a centralized merchandise planning and forecasting group to ensure consistent execution across omnichannel platforms and a planogram team that supports product placement. In stores, products are presented in an open-sell environment using centrally produced planograms and promotional merchandising planners. The planogram team works with merchants and inventory teams to ensure timely entry of new products, with major categories undergoing regular planogram revisions to adjust assortment mix and placement based on sales trends. The visual team collaborates with merchandising to develop strategic placement of promotional merchandise, functional and educational signage, and creative product presentation standards, with all stores receiving centrally produced promotional merchandising planners. We have a disciplined buying approach and a dynamic inventory planning and allocation process, centrally managed through a merchandise planning group that serves as a strategic partner and provides financial oversight to the merchandising team. The merchandising team creates annual category sales forecasts, and the planning group develops an open-to-buy plan for each category, approved by senior executives, which is updated weekly using point-of-sale (POS) data, receipts, and inventory levels to balance buying opportunities and inventory return on investment. This structure maximizes buying opportunities while maintaining financial and organizational control. POS data is used to calculate sales forecasts and determine replenishment levels, with promotional replenishment based on sales history from similar events. Weekly monitoring by the planning and replenishment group and senior executives tracks clearance and aged inventory levels. Our top ten brand partners, including L’Oréal and Estée Lauder Companies, accounted for 56% and 54% of total net sales in fiscal 2022 and the fiscal year ended January 29, 2022 (fiscal 2021), respectively. We maintain strong relationships with brand partners, who view us as a key distribution channel for growth and brand enhancement, and we work closely with them to market new and existing brands. All brand partners and their subcontractors must comply with Ulta Vendor Standards covering ethical, legal, social, and workplace requirements. Many have committed to advancing our mission of environmental sustainability by offering sustainable packaging, and we have committed to having 50% of product packaging sold at our stores be recyclable, refillable, or made from recycled or bio-sourced materials by 2025. Our marketing strategy includes print advertising, digital and social media, television, and radio to increase brand awareness, drive traffic to stores, website, and mobile apps, acquire new loyalty members, improve guest retention, increase shopping frequency, and boost spend per member. Our public relations strategy enhances Ulta Beauty’s reputation as a beauty destination, supports charitable efforts through the Ulta Beauty Charitable Foundation, and raises awareness of new products, in-store events, and store openings. The Ultamate Rewards loyalty program increases guest retention and loyalty, with CRM data enabling personalized marketing and day-to-day communications. Loyalty members spend more per visit than non-members. Points are earned from purchases at stores, digital platforms, and Ulta Beauty at Target, are valid for at least one year, and can be redeemed on any product or service. To enhance the program, we offer co-branded and private label credit cards that increase wallet share, loyalty, and consumer insights, and we expand our gift card program across store and online channels through third-party partnerships. We are increasing marketing spend toward digital, social media, and streaming advertising, which we believe effectively engages existing guests and drives consideration among new ones. Our digital marketing includes search engine optimization, paid search, mobile advertising, social media, display advertising, and other digital channels, combined with national TV and radio advertising to increase brand awareness and attract new guests. We have a deep understanding of Ultamate Rewards members and their preferences, supported by data analytics and CRM capabilities, enabling personalized experiences and new ways to support brand partners. In May 2022, we launched UB Media, a retail media network that allows brand partners to connect with beauty enthusiasts through personalized guest engagement and new guest acquisition. Retail stores are typically staffed with a general manager, services manager, three associate managers, and approximately 28 full- and part-time associates, including four to eight prestige consultants and five to ten licensed salon professionals. Store management reports to the General Manager, who oversees all store activities including salon management, inventory, merchandising, cash management, scheduling, hiring, and guest services. Management bonuses are based on position and performance metrics. Each General Manager reports to a District Manager, who reports to a Regional Vice President of Operations, who reports to a Senior Vice President of Stores, who reports to the Chief Operating Officer, who reports to the Chief Executive Officer. Store teams receive support from recruiting specialists, regionally based talent development managers, field loss prevention teams, service district educators and leaders, and brand partners. Stores are open seven days a week, typically eleven hours Monday through Saturday and seven hours on Sunday, with extended hours during the holiday season. A typical salon has five to ten licensed salon professionals, including six or more stylists, and some have an esthetician. Our most productive salons include a guest coordinator and assistant manager. Approximately 6,800 Ulta Beauty salon professionals participate in an educational program led by services district educators and brand partner education classes. Our vision is to build a dynamic, agile end-to-end supply chain that improves operational efficiency and guest experience. We operate four distribution centers supporting both stores and e-commerce, two fast fulfillment centers for e-commerce only, and 115 stores that fulfill e-commerce orders through our ship-from-store program. Starting in fiscal 2023, we will introduce market fulfillment centers focused on high-performing products to support e-commerce and store demand, especially in high-density markets. Inventory is shipped from suppliers to distribution and fast fulfillment centers, with replenishment primarily in eches (less-than-case quantities) to meet small needs. Distribution centers and fast fulfillment centers use warehouse management software to manage inventory and support purchase decisions. Products are delivered to stores via a network of contract and local pool carriers. As of January 28, 2023, we employed 18,500 full-time and 34,500 part-time associates, totaling 53,000 associates. We have no collective bargaining agreements and have not experienced work stoppages, believing we maintain good relationships with associates. Our goal is to create an inclusive environment where every associate can be authentic and every guest is served equitably. We achieve this through education on lived experiences, cultural moments, and unconscious bias, using a cross-functional DEI approach led by the Chief Executive Officer. We implement inclusive recruitment, celebrate intersectionality, encourage daily inclusive actions, and run a diverse leaders program. We ensure equitable in-store experiences through quarterly mandatory training for associates and weekly sessions focused on guest perspectives. In fiscal 2022, associates participated in Inclusion in Action training to reinforce inclusivity and address unconscious bias. As of January 28, 2023, key diversity metrics are: Women (55% board, 66% leadership, 91% associates), Men (45% board, 34% leadership, 9% associates), People of color (36% board, 27% leadership, 53% associates). The Chief Human Resources Officer and executive team develop and execute the human capital strategy, including talent attraction, acquisition, development, engagement, and compensation and benefits. Human capital objectives, including compensation policies, management development, DEI practices, and code of conduct compliance, are overseen by individual Board committees. We believe open and honest two-way communication is vital to associate engagement and conduct regular associate engagement surveys, which the executive team reviews. Leadership hosts roundtable sessions, department town halls, store and distribution center visits, and other small group gatherings. We are committed to attracting, training, retaining, and motivating qualified associates at all levels, with a focus on career advancement. We use a mix of existing managers, promoted associates, and outside hires to support store expansion, with most promotions being internal. All associates participate in an interactive new-hire orientation covering mission, vision, and values. Through a learning management system and digital workplace, associates receive ongoing education. A leadership development program prepares future leaders for new responsibilities. Our benefits include health care coverage for those working over 30 hours per week, extending to eligible dependents, comprehensive medical plans with choice, a 401(k) plan with up to a 4% company match, disability and life insurance, company-paid short-term disability at 80% of pay, additional insurance options (legal, pet, home, auto), tuition reimbursement, paid time off including an extended illness bank, and discounts on retail products and salon services. We also offer mental health resources, financial wellness planning, health mobile apps, and resources for soon-to-be parents. The Ulta Beauty Charitable Foundation supports the Associate Relief Program, which provides short-term financial assistance for medical bills or temporary housing. We operate with environmental responsibility, focusing on energy reduction in stores through safe indoor air, energy-efficient lighting, temperature management, and efficient water use in salons. We continue to reduce our carbon footprint through investments in renewable energy credits and collaboration with brand partners to reduce Scope 3 emissions. We rely on a variety of information systems and technologies, including cloud technologies, to manage operations across supply chain, merchandising, POS, e-commerce, marketing, finance, accounting, and human resources. Our core systems are a combination of purchased software and internally developed solutions, connected via a company-wide network that enables real-time polling of sales and merchandise movement. Data security and privacy are managed at the highest levels, with the Board of Directors actively overseeing cybersecurity, including through the Audit Committee. The Chief Information Officer and Chief Executive Officer keep the Board informed, and our Security Operations Center continuously monitors for threats. We have established data sharing processes, third-party risk assessments, regular disaster recovery planning, and response testing, with multiple layers of defense and control testing. We have strengthened data protection through investments and training, and all associates are trained as data stewards. As part of annual code of business conduct training, associates learn how to protect devices and data in public, avoid security threats and phishing, maintain secure workplaces, and follow everyday security practices. We plan to leverage technology to gain operational efficiencies through better use of systems, people, and processes. In fiscal 2021, we began a multi-year upgrade of our enterprise resource planning platform to create a flexible and scalable environment for greater business efficiency. We continue to invest in information systems to support growth and enhance competitiveness. We have registered trademarks in the United States and other countries, with most registrations containing the ULTA mark, including Ulta Beauty, Ulta.com, Ulta Salon, Cosmetics & Fragrance (and design). We maintain and monitor renewal deadlines for all marks deemed material to our business, with applications or registrations in the U.S. and select foreign countries including Canada, Mexico, and other countries in Latin America, Europe, and Asia. We believe our trademarks, especially those related to the Ulta Beauty brand, “All Things Beauty. All In One Place. ®”, “The Possibilities are Beautiful®”, “21 Days of Beauty®”, and “, are critical to our brand identity.

We intend to use our technology infrastructure and systems to improve operational efficiency by optimizing the use of our systems, people, and processes. In fiscal 2021, we initiated a multi-year upgrade of our enterprise resource planning platform, which will create a flexible and scalable operating environment to enhance business efficiency. We will continue to invest in our information systems to support growth and strengthen our competitive position. We have registered trademarks in the United States and other countries, with the majority of these registrations featuring the ULTA mark, including Ulta Beauty, two related designs, Ulta.com, and Ulta Salon, Cosmetics & Fragrance (and design). We actively maintain and monitor renewal deadlines for these marks and have applied for or registered all marks deemed material to our business in the United States and select foreign countries, including Canada, Mexico, and other countries in Latin America, Europe, and Asia. We believe our trademarks, particularly those associated with the Ulta Beauty brand—such as “All Things Beauty. All In One Place. ®”, “The Possibilities are Beautiful®”, “21 Days of Beauty®”, and “Conscious Beauty at Ulta Beauty®”—hold significant value and are essential for building brand recognition. Our business is subject to extensive federal, state, and local laws, regulations, administrative determinations, and court decisions. Products sold, including cosmetics (including those with cannabidiol), dietary supplements, food, over-the-counter (OTC) drugs, medical devices, and styling tools, including Ulta Beauty-branded items, are regulated by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC), the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), state regulatory agencies, and State Attorneys General. These regulations primarily address safety, labeling, manufacturing, advertising, and distribution. Salon services in our stores are also subject to state and local regulations. Cosmetics, OTC drugs, medical devices, and dietary supplements have specific regulatory requirements related to ingredients, labeling, manufacturing, and holding. Products like wrinkle-reducing lights may be classified as medical devices and are subject to premarket review by the FDA in addition to labeling and manufacturing requirements. Styling tools, such as blow dryers and curling irons, are regulated by the CPSC, which enforces strict requirements, including mandatory reporting of certain product defects. All product labeling and packaging are subject to the Fair Packaging and Labeling Act and state-specific rules. Advertising statements about product safety or efficacy, pricing, or environmental claims are subject to federal and state consumer protection laws that prohibit unfair or deceptive practices. We are also subject to labor and employment laws, taxation laws, governmental and real estate land use restrictions, and advertising and consumer protection laws at federal, state, municipal, and local levels. Our services operations are subject to state board regulations and licensing requirements. In store leases, we require landlords to obtain necessary governmental approvals and permits for the site and for our specific use, though in some cases we are responsible for securing these permits. We require landlords to provide a certificate of occupancy for any work performed on our buildings or shopping centers, and if required by the municipality, we are responsible for delivering a certificate of occupancy for any remodeling or build-outs and for complying with all applicable laws related to such projects. Our business experiences seasonal fluctuations, with significant net sales and profits realized during the fourth quarter due to the holiday selling season, and to a lesser extent, during Mother’s Day and Valentine’s Day. Our principal website is www.ulta.com, where under investor relations (at https://ulta.com/investor), we provide free of charge our proxy statement, annual report to shareholders, annual report on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and all amendments to these reports as soon as reasonably practicable after filing with or furnishing to the SEC. Information on our website is not incorporated by reference and is not deemed part of this Form 10-K. Our SEC filings are accessible via www.sec.gov. All statements in our filings, including forward-looking statements, are made as of the date of the document and we do not undertake any obligation to update them unless required by law. Key risks include the possibility that we may fail to implement our long-range strategic, operational, and financial plans, which could negatively impact our business, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. Our growth depends on our ability to open and operate new stores profitably and to anticipate and respond to changing consumer preferences, including those related to sustainability, ingredient transparency, and animal welfare. If we fail to recognize beauty trends or react to shifting consumer preferences, our sales could decline. We also depend on our ability to translate market trends into timely, saleable product and service offerings, maintain vendor relationships, and efficiently distribute merchandise. Failure to meet consumer merchandise needs could reduce net sales and increase markdowns, harming our business. Any significant interruption in the operations of our distribution and fast fulfillment centers could disrupt timely delivery to stores, negatively affecting our operations. We distribute products without relying on direct-to-store vendor arrangements and carry over 25,000 beauty products that frequently change with trends, making our operations vulnerable to supply chain disruptions. Disruptions from information system failures, fires, natural disasters, labor disputes, inventory shortages, or shipping issues could severely limit our ability to deliver products and services. Rising shipping and transportation costs due to inflation could also harm our business. Our e-commerce platform, which includes sales through Ulta.com and mobile applications, exposes us to risks such as difficulty in attracting and retaining customers, challenges in operating and developing digital systems, and potential conflicts between product offerings across channels. If our e-commerce platform grows by attracting existing customers rather than new ones, it could reduce store revenues. Offering different products through online and in-store channels may lead to customer confusion or cause vendors to consider competing digital platforms. As omnichannel retailing evolves, we must adapt to changing guest expectations and competitive developments. Failure to develop or improve guest-facing technology in a timely manner could harm our competitiveness and results. Increased costs or interruptions in overseas sourcing from third-party vendors could disrupt production, shipment, or receipt of merchandise, leading to lost sales and higher costs. We source most of our Ulta Beauty branded components and gifts through foreign factories via third-party vendors, many of whom use overseas manufacturing. Disruptions from import restrictions, geopolitical events, political changes, increased duties, or legal/economic restrictions could severely impact our supply chain and operations. We have no long-term supply contracts for these foreign-sourced items, which are subject to duties, tariffs, or quotas that may limit imports. Risks include political instability, labor disputes, local business practices, health concerns from infectious diseases, adverse weather, natural disasters, or acts of war or terrorism affecting production or shipment. Our business depends heavily on strong relationships with brand partners to obtain prestige, mass, and salon beauty products on reasonable terms and to offer exclusive or limited-time products. Without these relationships, we may not secure sufficient product selection or volume, or respond promptly to market trends. We have no long-term supply agreements with brand partners, and some prestige partners may not have the capacity to meet our growth needs. Strategic partnerships with core brands have helped us benefit from their popularity, but any of these brands could end or scale back their partnership, negatively impacting revenue. During fiscal 2022 and fiscal 2021, merchandise from our top ten brand partners accounted for approximately 56% and 54% of net sales, respectively. Vendor consolidation in the beauty industry increases the risk that losing or reducing supply from any key vendor could harm our business. If brand partners stop granting us permanent or temporary exclusivity, our net sales could decline. We also face inventory shrinkage risks due to damage, theft (including organized retail crime), and other causes, with elevated levels recently affecting our results. To combat rising shrink, we have taken and may continue to take operational and strategic actions that could harm our reputation and guest experience. Our comparable sales and quarterly financial performance fluctuate due to various factors, including general U.S. economic conditions, merchandising strategy, performance of new stores, inventory management, timing of store openings, cannibalization, marketing effectiveness, seasonal trends, competitor actions, and natural disasters or pandemics. These fluctuations mean that results in one quarter are not indicative of future performance, and a decline in comparable sales could lead to a drop in the price of our common stock. Our distribution and order fulfillment infrastructure, currently consisting of four distribution centers and two fast fulfillment centers, may not be sufficient to support future growth. Failure to timely expand or upgrade this infrastructure could prevent successful implementation of growth plans and result in excess costs, negatively affecting our business, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. Our results also depend on the effectiveness of our marketing, advertising, and promotional programs, which influence customer traffic and demand. Disruptions to media channels could harm our operations. Additionally, the increased use of social media platforms allows for widespread negative commentary about us or our products, which could damage our reputation.

It is likely that additional distribution facilities will be added in the future. If the company fails to effectively upgrade and expand its distribution capacity in a timely manner to keep pace with anticipated store growth and distribution center performance, this could have a material adverse effect on its business, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. Unsuccessful marketing, advertising, and promotional programs could also adversely affect its results of operations and financial condition. Customer traffic and demand are influenced by advertising, marketing, and promotional activities, which the company uses across various media, including social media, websites, mobile applications, email, and print. Future growth and profitability depend in part on the effectiveness and efficiency of these programs; disruptions to certain media channels could have a material adverse effect. The use of social media may harm the company’s reputation, as negative commentary about the company or its products can be posted at any time and may be acted upon by customers without further investigation or regard for accuracy. Customers value readily available information, and such harm may be immediate with no opportunity for redress. The company maintains Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, TikTok, and Pinterest accounts as marketing tools, and failure by the company, its employees, or third parties acting on its behalf to comply with evolving laws and regulations governing these platforms could adversely impact its business, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. Failure to retain existing senior management or attract qualified new personnel at all levels could have a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. The company’s operations require disciplined execution, which depends on an experienced and talented management team; losing key executive personnel could have a material adverse effect. The company must continue to train, motivate, and manage associates and also attract, motivate, and retain qualified executive, managerial, merchandising personnel, and store and distribution center associates, as competition for such personnel is intense, especially due to labor pressures from the COVID-19 pandemic, and the company may not succeed in attracting, assimilating, or retaining the needed personnel. Fluctuations in labor costs, including those driven by inflationary wage pressures, may negatively impact profitability and cash flows. The company has a $1.0 billion secured revolving credit facility with a term expiring in March 2025, where substantially all of its assets are pledged as collateral. The agreement includes usual and customary restrictive covenants that limit the company’s ability to incur additional debt, pay cash dividends, repurchase stock, or merge or consolidate, and require maintenance of a fixed charge coverage ratio of at least 1.0 to 1.0 when availability falls below a specified threshold. These covenants could restrict operational flexibility, and failure to comply or meet payment obligations would limit borrowing and, in certain cases, allow lenders to require repayment. Macroeconomic conditions, including inflation, rising interest rates, recessionary concerns, labor cost pressures, transportation and shipping cost pressures, and the ongoing impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, have negatively affected and may continue to affect the company’s business, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. For example, fiscal 2022 was negatively impacted by persistent cost pressures, including supply chain and labor costs, and inflationary cost pressures are expected to continue in 2023. The company closely monitors macroeconomic conditions, including customer behavior, and ongoing inflation, recessionary concerns, supply chain and labor challenges, and banking industry turmoil could have a material adverse impact. Although the company has no operations outside the United States, geopolitical events such as the Russia-Ukraine conflict and related sanctions have increased global economic uncertainty and exacerbated inflation. Economic conditions may affect consumer purchases of discretionary items like beauty products and salon services, which could have a material adverse effect. The company’s results may be materially affected by capital market and general economic conditions, as it appeals to a broad demographic and offers an extensive selection of beauty products and premium salon services. Uncertainty in the economy could reduce consumer purchases of discretionary items across all product categories, including prestige beauty and premium salon services, due to factors such as general business conditions, inflation, interest rates, employment levels, tax rates, consumer credit availability, confidence in future economic conditions, and risks from epidemics or geopolitical events. A prolonged period of inflation, economic downturn, or recession could adversely affect consumer spending habits, leading to lower-than-expected net sales. A general deterioration in economic conditions could also harm commercial partners, including brand partners, real estate developers, and landlords who operate or develop retail centers where the company’s stores are located. A bankruptcy or financial failure of a significant vendor or major real estate developer or landlord could have a material adverse effect. Volatility and disruption in capital and credit markets could negatively impact global economic conditions, leading to inflationary or recessionary pressures, reduced consumer confidence, and economic growth, which may result in lower consumer spending. Reduced spending could alter customer order patterns and merchandise purchases, signaling a reset in consumer habits, all of which could adversely affect the business, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. The company may be unable to compete effectively in its highly competitive markets, where few barriers exist. It competes against a diverse group of retailers, including regional and national department stores, specialty retailers, drug stores, mass merchandisers, high-end and discount salon chains, locally owned beauty retailers, online capabilities of national retailers, pure-play e-commerce companies, catalog retailers, and direct response television. The company believes its main competitive advantages are the breadth of merchandise, value proposition, quality of the shopping experience, and store convenience as one-stop destinations. Many competitors are larger and have greater financial, marketing, and other resources, enabling them to adapt more quickly, invest more in marketing, generate greater brand recognition, or adopt more aggressive pricing, which could result in loss of market share and a material adverse effect. A reduction in traffic to, or the closing of, other destination retailers in shopping areas where the company’s stores are located could significantly reduce sales and lead to excess inventory, which could have a material adverse effect. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Overview: We were founded in 1990 as a beauty retailer at a time when prestige, mass, and salon products were sold through distinct channels – department stores for prestige products; drug stores and mass merchandisers for mass products; and salons and authorized retail outlets for professional hair care products. We developed a unique specialty retail concept that offers a broad range of brands and price points, select beauty services, and a convenient and welcoming shopping environment. We define our target consumer as a beauty enthusiast, a consumer who is passionate about the beauty category, uses beauty for self-expression, experimentation, and self-investment, and has high expectations for the shopping experience. We estimate beauty enthusiasts represent approximately 65% of shoppers and 80% of beauty products and services spend in the U.S. We believe our strategy provides us with the competitive advantages that have contributed to our financial performance. Today, we are the largest specialty beauty retailer in the United States and the premier beauty destination for cosmetics, fragrance, skin care products, hair care products, and salon services. Key aspects of our business include: a differentiated assortment of more than 25,000 beauty products across a variety of categories and price points as well as a variety of beauty services, including salon services, in more than 1,350 stores predominantly located in convenient, high-traffic locations; engaging digital experiences delivered through our website, Ulta.com, and our mobile applications; our best-in-class loyalty program that enables members to earn points for every dollar spent on products and beauty services and provides us with deep, proprietary customer insights; and our ability to cultivate human connection with warm and welcoming guest experiences across all of our channels. The continued growth of our business and any future increases in net sales, net income, and cash flows is dependent on our ability to execute our strategic priorities: 1) drive breakthrough and disruptive growth through an expanded definition of All Things Beauty; 2) evolve the omnichannel experience through connected physical and digital ecosystems, All In Your World; 3) expand and deepen our presence across the beauty journey, solidifying Ulta Beauty at the Heart of the Beauty Community; 4) drive operational excellence and optimization; 5) protect and cultivate our world-class culture and talent; and 6) expand our environmental and social impact. We believe the attractive and growing U.S. beauty products and salon services industry, the expanding definition of beauty and the role that omnichannel capabilities play in consumers’ lives, coupled with Ulta Beauty’s competitive strengths, position us to capture additional market share in the industry. Comparable sales is a key metric that is monitored closely within the retail industry. Our comparable sales have fluctuated in the past, and we expect them to continue to fluctuate in the future. A variety of factors affect our comparable sales, including general U.S. economic conditions, changes in merchandise strategy or mix, and timing and effectiveness of our marketing activities, among others. Over the long term, our growth strategy is to increase total net sales through growing our comparable sales, expanding omnichannel capabilities, and opening new stores. Long-term operating profit is expected to increase as a result of our efforts to optimize our real estate portfolio, expand merchandise margin, and leverage our fixed store costs with comparable sales increases and operating efficiencies, partially offset by incremental investments in people, guest experiences, systems, and supply chain required to support a 1,500 to 1,700 store chain in the U.S. with successful e-commerce and competitive omnichannel capabilities. Current Trends: Impact of COVID-19: We closely monitor the continuing impact of COVID-19 on all facets of our business. While operations during fiscal 2022 did not appear to be negatively impacted, the COVID-19 pandemic and the conditions and trends that originated during the pandemic could have negative impacts in the future. The extent of the impact of the pandemic and the conditions and trends that originated during the pandemic on our future business and financial results will depend on, among other things, the potential of temporary restrictions on operating hours, in-store services or reclosing of certain stores or other facilities of ours or our brand partners and other suppliers, supply chain disruptions, increased transportation and shipping costs, higher wholesale costs, increased labor costs, and the duration, timing and severity of the impact of the foregoing on consumer spending. Industry trends: Our research indicates that Ulta Beauty has captured meaningful market share across all categories over the last several years. However, the COVID-19 pandemic and its various impacts changed consumer behavior and consumption of beauty products, at least temporarily, due to the closures of offices, retail stores, and other businesses and the significant decline in travel, entertainment and social gatherings. The overall beauty market declined in 20.

The company closely monitors the ongoing impact of COVID-19 on its business, noting that operations during fiscal 2022 were not negatively affected, but future impacts—such as temporary restrictions on operating hours, in-store services, or store closures, supply chain disruptions, increased transportation and shipping costs, higher wholesale and labor costs, and changes in consumer spending—could still pose risks. The pandemic altered consumer behavior temporarily due to store and office closures and reduced travel and social activities, leading to a decline in the overall beauty market in 2020, stabilization in 2021, and growth in 2022 as consumers resumed in-person shopping while maintaining some online habits. The company remains confident in its long-term market share gains due to its differentiated business model, strategic investments, and engaged associates. The company has one reportable segment encompassing retail stores, salon services, and e-commerce. Revenue is recognized at the point of sale in retail stores, upon shipment or guest pickup for e-commerce, net of estimated returns, with shipping and handling treated as fulfillment costs. Salon service revenue is recognized when provided, gift card revenue is deferred until redemption, company coupons and incentives are recorded as a reduction of net sales, and other revenue includes private label and co-branded credit card programs, Target royalties, and deferred revenue from the loyalty program and gift card breakage. Comparable sales, which begin on the first day of the 14th month of store operation, include retail, salon, and e-commerce sales and exclude new stores not yet in their 13th month or those closed for part or all of the period; remodeled stores are included unless closed during the period. Factors affecting comparable sales include economic conditions, new product launches, store locations, competition, responsiveness to consumer preferences, marketing effectiveness, and the number of new stores opened. Cost of sales includes merchandise costs, vendor income, distribution costs, shipping, retail occupancy, salon payroll, and shrink and inventory reserves. Selling, general, and administrative expenses include payroll, advertising (offset by vendor reimbursements), corporate occupancy, stock-based compensation, depreciation (excluding retail and distribution assets), and corporate overhead. Impairment, restructuring, and other costs include long-lived asset impairments, store closing costs, suspension of the Canadian expansion, and severance. Pre-opening expenses cover rent, setup labor, training, and grand opening advertising for new, remodeled, or relocated stores. Interest (income) expense, net includes interest from short-term investments and interest on the credit facility, which is structured as an asset-based lending instrument with a variable rate that can increase during rising interest rates. Net sales increased to $10,208,580 in fiscal 2022 from $8,630,889 in fiscal 2021, a rise of $1.6 billion or 18.3%, driven by the beauty category’s resilience, retail price increases, new brands, product innovation, more social occasions, fewer pandemic limitations, and $77.3 million in other revenue. Comparable sales rose 15.6% in fiscal 2022 versus 37.9% in fiscal 2021, driven by a 10.8% increase in transactions and a 4.3% increase in average ticket. Selling, general, and administrative expenses increased to $2,395,299 in fiscal 2022 from $2,061,545 in fiscal 2021, a $333.8 million or 16.2% increase, with the percentage of net sales decreasing to 23.5% from 23.9% due to 80 basis points from lower marketing and 20 basis points from higher sales incentive compensation, partially offset by 40 basis points of corporate overhead deleverage and 20 basis points of store payroll deleverage. In fiscal 2021, net sales increased to $8,630,889 from $6,151,953 in fiscal 2020, a $2.5 billion or 40.3% rise, due to stronger consumer confidence, government stimulus, easing pandemic restrictions, and $15.1 million in other revenue.
